Company Description

Join us and make YOUR mark on the World!

Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) has turned bold ideas into world-changing impact advancing science and technology to strengthen U.S. security and promote global stability.

Our mission spans four critical national security areas nuclear deterrence, threat preparedness, energy security, and multi-domain defense empowering teams to take on the toughest challenges of today and tomorrow. With a culture built on innovation and operational excellence, LLNL is a place where your expertise can make a real impact.

Job Description

We're looking for an Environmental Data Specialist.
You will perform data entry and data management following established business processes to retrieve, verify, and maintain data generated during environmental site characterization, remediation, and monitoring activities. Work with database users, technical field teams, and contract laboratories to receive, assess, and process data; enhance data integrity, accessibility, and usability across one or more functional areas. The position is in the Program Services & Operations Division of the Environmental Restoration Department (ERD).

This position may offer a hybrid schedule, which includes the flexibility to work from home one or more days per week, after a probationary period. The specifics of the hybrid schedule, including the exact number of days required in the office and virtual work options may vary based on the needs of the team and the organization.

You will

Perform data entry and data management following established business processes to retrieve, verify and maintain data generated during environmental site characterization, remediation, and monitoring activities.
Collaborate with stakeholders to define data requirements, reporting needs, and document them in clear specifications.
Work with technical staff to troubleshoot data issues, coordinate testing, and validate changes or enhancements to data systems and interfaces.
Develop and produce standard, recurring, and ad hoc reports, including data validation and explanation of trends or anomalies.
Assist in designing and implementing improvements to data collection, storage, and retrieval processes, including configuration of data management tools or applications.
Contribute to data-management documentation, including data dictionaries, standard operating procedures, records archives, and data-repositories, and support user training on data-entry standards, reporting tools, and data-management best practices.
Ensure chain-of-custody (COC) forms are complete, accurate, and timely and that the data from the analytical laboratories adhere to the contract.
Monitor data quality metrics and assist in developing controls, checks, and procedures to ensure accuracy, consistency, and completeness of data.
Assist in developing environmental sampling plans and contributing to environmental regulatory reports.
Perform Technical Release Representative (TRR) duties to release work to outside vendors, commit substantial financial resources, and process and pay subcontract analytical laboratory invoices.
Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

Ability to secure and maintain a U.S. DOE Q-level security clearance which requires U.S. citizenship.
Bachelor’s degree in business, or related field, or equivalent combination of education and related experience.
Extensive knowledge of and experience with data management systems related to data entry and verification.
Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, accuracy, and follow through; experience with techniques for maintaining data integrity, error cause and effect analysis, and error prevention.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with experience to anticipate, identify, and resolve complex problems effectively.
Experience analyzing electronic data deliverables and creating standard and ad hoc reports.
Proven written and verbal communication skills necessary for effective interactions with all levels of personnel internal and external, regulatory agencies, and vendors, and experience working effectively independently and as a member of a team.
Knowledge of and experience using computer programs, system software and computer equipment, such as Microsoft Excel, Oracle based applications, SQL, Apple/Mac, and Linux operating systems.

Qualifications We Desire

Knowledge of LLNL procurement policies and procedures and best business practices.
Experience working with TEIMS, knowledge of SPACT, and ERD’s data repositories (i.e. Data Cave and Data Alley) and LLNL Records Management.
Familiarity with chemistry nomenclature to understand analytical laboratory test results.

Pay Range

$95,820 - $117,312 Annually

This is the lowest to highest salary we in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. An employee’s position within the salary range will be based on several factors including, but not limited to, specific competencies, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, seniority, geographic location, performance, and business or organizational needs.

Additional Information

Position Information

This is a Career Indefinite position, open to Lab employees and external candidates.

Why Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory?

Included in 2026 Best Places to Work by Glassdoor!
Flexible Benefits Package
401(k)
Relocation Assistance
Education Reimbursement Program
Flexible schedules (*depending on project needs)
Our values - visit https://www.llnl.gov/inclusion/our-values

Security Clearance

This position requires a Department of Energy (DOE) Q-level clearance. If you are selected, we will initiate a Federal background investigation to determine if you meet eligibility requirements for access to classified information or matter. Also, all L or Q cleared employees are subject to random drug testing. Q-level clearance requires U.S. citizenship.

Pre-Employment Drug Test

External applicant(s) selected for this position must pass a post-offer, pre-employment drug test. This includes testing for use of marijuana as Federal Law applies to us as a Federal Contractor.

Wireless and Medical Devices

Per the Department of Energy (DOE), Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory must meet certain restrictions with the use and/or possession of mobile devices in Limited Areas. Depending on your job duties, you may be required to work in a Limited Area where you are not permitted to have a personal and/or laboratory mobile device in your possession. If you use a medical device, which pairs with a mobile device, you must still follow the rules concerning the mobile device in individual sections within Limited Areas. Technical Product Management

Job Category

Scientific/Technology

All Job Posting Locations:

La Jolla, California, United States of America, Spring House, Pennsylvania, United States of America

Job Description

Johnson & Johnson Innovative Medicine is recruiting for a Technical Product Owner – Toxicology Systems
, located in Spring House, PA (US), La Jolla, CA (US) or Beerse, Belgium.

Please note that this role is available across multiple countries and may be posted under different requisition numbers to comply with local requirements. While you are welcome to apply to any or all of the postings, we recommend focusing on the specific country(s) that align with your preferred location(s):

United States (Spring House or La Jolla) - Requisition Number: R-094926
Belgium (Beerse) - Requisition Number: R-096026

The Technology Product Owner for Toxicology will own the technical delivery and support of toxicology products directly supporting toxicology and compound promiscuity science. This business technology role combines deep domain and technical expertise with program-level coordination: you will define technical strategy, own roadmaps and delivery for platforms and models used by toxicology scientists, and act as the primary technical partner and escalation point for scientific stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities

Lead the technology strategy, roadmap, prioritization, and delivery for digital products supporting toxicology workflows, aligning scientific needs, enterprise technology standards, and available delivery capacity.
Translate scientific needs into technical requirements, success criteria, and measurable deliverables; ensure clear acceptance criteria and productization pathways.
Provide hands-on technical leadership when it adds the most value, including architecture definition, rapid prototyping, design reviews, and evaluation of pipelines and models; coordinate delivery across engineering, data, quality, and scientific partner teams.
Ensure robust data ingestion, normalization, annotation, and QC processes; drive integrations with LIMS, ELN, assay instruments, and third-party data providers.
Define and promote fit-for-purpose practices for data provenance, metadata standards, FAIR principles, and auditability to support scientific reproducibility and applicable compliance requirements.
Act as primary technical liaison for toxicology scientists: capture requirements, demo solutions, gather feedback, and drive adoption.
Lead technical evaluations of vendors and third-party solutions, provide due diligence and risk assessments, and coordinate integrations with procurement, legal, cybersecurity, quality, and engineering partners.
Communicate product status, value, trade-offs, dependencies, and technical risks to leadership and cross-functional stakeholders; facilitate decisions and escalate issues when appropriate.

Qualifications

Required:

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Bioinformatics, Computational Chemistry, Toxicology, or related field required; Master’s or PhD preferred.
5+ years of experience supporting scientific research platforms
Demonstrated depth in designing, delivering, and sustaining data platforms, analytics products, or machine learning solutions in life sciences, drug discovery, or another complex scientific environment.
Demonstrated track record of leading technical programs or major projects end-to-end in a complex organization.
Scientific literacy in toxicology and compound promiscuity concepts: assay types, ADME endpoints and off-target profiling.
Maintain sufficient software and data engineering depth to guide solution design, evaluate implementation quality, and contribute directly when needed, including experience with Python or R, SQL, REST APIs, containerization, CI/CD practices, and cloud environments.
Systems and architecture skills: ability to design scalable, maintainable platforms that meet scientists’ needs and regulatory constraints.
Product and delivery leadership: define product outcomes, shape roadmaps, prioritize investments, establish success measures, manage dependencies and risks, and align cross-functional partners around delivery decisions.
Operational leadership: establish support models, service expectations, lifecycle plans, and escalation paths for production solutions; use reliability, adoption, quality, and value measures to guide continuous improvement.
Executive-ready communication and influence: explain technical choices, business value, delivery trade-offs, and risk to scientific, technology, and leadership audiences; build alignment and drive decisions without direct authority.
Strong problem-solving mindset and bias for pragmatic, evidence-driven solutions.

Preferred

Advanced degree (MS/PhD) in toxicology, cheminformatics, computational chemistry, or related discipline.
Hands-on experience with cheminformatics tooling (e.g., RDKit), molecular representations, fingerprints, SMARTS/substructure filtering, and selectivity/promiscuity scoring approaches.
Experience with ML libraries and frameworks (scikit-learn, TensorFlow, PyTorch) and MLOps tools (model registries, monitoring).
Prior experience in regulated or GLP-relevant environments, or with quality frameworks that apply to scientific data and software.
Experience performing technical vendor evaluations and managing third-party scientific data/software integrations.

jobs.description:
**Company Description** **Work with Us. Change the World.**


At AECOM, we're delivering a better world. Whether improving your commute, keeping the lights on, providing access to clean water, or transforming skylines, our work helps people and communities thrive. We are the world's trusted infrastructure consulting firm, partnering with clients to solve the world’s most complex challenges and build legacies for future generations.


There has never been a better time to be at AECOM. With accelerating infrastructure investment worldwide, our services are in great demand. We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of over 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world.


We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.

 **Job Description** **AECOM's** **Environment, Health \& Safety team** is seeking an experienced **Mid\-level Environmental Scientist III** to join our team and support and manage environmental compliance programs for public\- and/or private\-sector clients. This mid\-level role is ideal for a candidate with a solid regulatory foundation who can work independently on routine compliance tasks while supporting more complex projects under senior staff guidance. The successful candidate will contribute to technical delivery, client support, and internal collaboration within a consulting\-oriented environment.

**This hybrid position will be based out of our San Jose, CA office.**

**Key Responsibilities include:**

* Environmental Compliance Support.
* Support implementation of environmental compliance programs related to federal, state, and local regulations (e.g., Clean Air Act, Clean Water Act, RCRA, TSCA, EPCRA, and state equivalents).
* Conduct regulatory applicability evaluations, document reviews, and compliance assessments.
* Assist with preparation of permit applications, compliance plans, reports, and regulatory correspondence.
* Support environmental audits and follow\-up corrective actions under direction of senior staff.
* Track regulatory changes and assist with compliance strategy updates.
* Project support \& client interaction.
* Provide day\-to\-day technical support for environmental compliance projects.
* Coordinate with project managers and multidisciplinary teams to meet scope, schedule, and quality requirements.
* Participate in client meetings and site visits as needed.
* Prepare clear, well\-organized technical deliverables and summaries for client review.
* Data Management \& Documentation
* Compile, manage, and analyze environmental compliance data.
* Support development and maintenance of compliance tracking tools and documentation systems.
* Ensure project files and records meet internal quality and compliance standards.

**About AECOM’s Environment Business Line**  

Join AECOM to be part of an expert global team who is connected through a well\-developed, worldwide, internal technical practice network through which you can learn from and brainstorm with the best in the world. AECOM is an industry\-leading, world class environmental firm, and we want you to succeed within it. We respect and encourage your own pathway to excellence via our Freedom to Grow initiative.  

  

AECOM is known for our award\-winning technical excellence, leading\-edge science and innovative project delivery. We provide sustainable solutions for some of the world’s most challenging issues. Our global clients and their projects span a variety of market sectors and geographies and require innovative technical solutions to solve wide\-ranging environmental problems.

 **Qualifications** **Minimum Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree in environmental science, environmental engineering, chemistry, or a related field.
* 4 years of relevant experience or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education focusing on environmental compliance within consulting, industry, or a regulatory agency with strong knowledge of key environmental regulations and compliance frameworks.
* Due to the nature of the work, US Citizenship is required.
* Valid Driver's license and motor vehicle records check is required for this role.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Master’s degree or professional certification (e.g., CHMM, CEA) is a plus.
* 6\+ years of relevant experience or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education focusing on environmental compliance within consulting, industry, or a regulatory agency with strong knowledge of key environmental regulations and compliance frameworks.
* Experience preparing technical reports and supporting environmental permitting or compliance activities.
* Prior experience working in an environmental consulting firm is highly desired.
* Familiarity with state environmental programs and agency interactions.
* Experience with compliance auditing, inspections, or regulatory inspections.
* Proficiency with compliance tracking tools, spreadsheets, or data management systems.
* Ability to manage multiple tasks and deadlines in a project\-based environment.

  

**Additional Information**  

At AECOM, we are committed to maintaining a secure and trustworthy recruitment process and take any fraudulent hiring activity seriously. ***To support this commitment, all newly hired employees are required to attend an in\-person Day 1 onboarding at an AECOM office location as a condition of employment.***

- Foster collaboration, knowledge sharing, and work-sharing across teams and regions
- Represent HDR through industry organizations, conference presentations, and community leadership activities
- Take on impactful project management and leadership assignments that align with HDR’s long-term growth strategy

jobs.description:
**Company Description**  

Eurofins Scientific is a network of independent companies providing a unique range of analytical testing  

services to clients across multiple industries, to make life and our environment safer, healthier and more sustainable. From the food you eat, to the water you drink, to the medicines you rely on, Eurofins laboratories work to ensure the products they supply are safe, their ingredients are authentic, and labelling is accurate.


Eurofins is dedicated to delivering testing services that contribute to the health and safety of society and the planet, and to its corporate responsibility to protect the environment and ensure diversity, equity, and inclusion across the entire network of Eurofins companies.


With over 50 laboratories and more than 40 service centers nationwide, Eurofins Environment Testing provides full\-service environmental analysis across all 50 states. Our network supports public and private clients—including DoD, DOE, and municipalities—through robust logistics and continuous investment in people, technology, and infrastructure. We offer comprehensive testing for air, water, soil, sediment, tissue, and waste, covering a wide range of analytes including PFAS, metals, VOCs/SVOCs, dioxins/furans, radiochemicals, and more.

 **Job Description**  

 Eurofins Drinking Water and Wastewater West in Pomona, CA is the largest and most recognized water and beverage testing laboratory in the United States, providing water quality compliance and specialty testing to more than 500 municipal, State and Federal customers.


 Eurofins Drinking Water and Wastewater West has a Scientist I opening at our Pomona Laboratory in the Metals department. This is a full time position, 40 hrs/week.


Duties include:

* Routine sample preparation and analysis of water samples by various written EPA and Standard Methods procedures,
* Performing data process, data entry and written documentation
* Performing routine instrument maintenance.
* Preparation of reagents and standards.
* Other general laboratory related duties as assigned
* Will include regular late shift and/or weekend duties.

  

**Qualifications**  

* Minimum BS/BA degree in chemistry and /or other related science field; one to two years of laboratory experience.
* One to two years of ICP\-OES and ICP\-MS (EPA 200\.7/EPA 200\.8\) experience preferred.
* Must be available to work overtime including weekends.
* Excellent math and computer skills
* Excellent written and communication skills
* Excellent attention to details and good organization skills
* Ability to work well independently as well as in a team environmen

  

**Additional Information**  

This is a full time position Tuesday to Saturday 9 am to 6 pm with possibility of overtime.

**Pay Rate Range for this position is** **$22\.20 \- $25 (DOE).**


Candidates within a commutable distance to Pomona, CA are encouraged to apply.


Eurofins Environment Testing (USA) provides a compensation range for informational purposes, the actual base salary may vary based upon, but not limited to, relevant experience and skill set, base salary of internal peers, business sector, and geographic location.


As a Eurofins employee, you will become part of a company that has received national recognition as a great place to work. We offer excellent full\-time benefits including comprehensive medical coverage, life and disability insurance, 401(k) with company match, paid holidays, paid time off, and dental and vision options.

**To learn more about Eurofins, please explore our website www.eurofinsus.com**

**We support your development!** Do you feel you don’t match 100% of the requirements? Don’t hesitate to apply anyway! Eurofins companies are committed to supporting your career development.

**We embrace diversity!** Eurofins network of companies believe in strength and innovation through diversity, being an Equal Opportunity Employer. We prohibit discrimination against employees or applications based on gender identity and/or expression, race, nationality, age, religion, sexual orientation, disability, and everything else that makes employees of Eurofins companies unique.

**Sustainability matters to us!** At Eurofins, we believe sustainability is at the heart of everything we do. Guided by our vision to be the Global Leader in “Testing for Life,” our mission to contribute to a healthier and safer world, and our core values, we are building a strong foundation for Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) initiatives. Eurofins’ commitment to sustainability begins within our own companies through a shared responsibility to people and the planet. With climate change posing an imminent threat, Eurofins and its many companies recognize their duty to proactively reduce or offset the environmental impact of essential operations while also helping our clients do the same—serving as a true ESG Enabler.

**Find out more in our career page: https://careers.eurofins.com/**

Become part of our dynamic Water business which boasts around 600 experts across Australia and New Zealand and 6000 globally. Collaborate with top-tier civil, mechanical, electrical, and process engineers to deliver a variety of captivating projects, from small initiatives to large-scale ventures, all the way from concept to completion. .

Job Description

Growth & Diverse Opportunities

AECOM's Water team is delivering some of the most significant water projects across Australia and New Zealand, backed by a record pipeline of work and the strength of our global network. From major flood resilience and water security programs to renewable energy, transport and critical infrastructure projects, our teams are helping shape more sustainable and resilient communities.

As we continue to grow, we're seeking talented Water Resources professionals who want to work on industry-leading projects, collaborate with experts across the globe, and build a rewarding long-term career with AECOM.

With opportunities coming up across Sydney, Melbourne, Adelaide, Brisbane, Perth, Newcastle, Gold Coast, Auckland, Wellington and Christchurch
, you can be based from flexible locations Australia and New Zealand offices while contributing to projects of regional, national and international significance.

Whether you're an emerging professional, an experienced technical specialist or an established leader, we offer the opportunity to work on complex, meaningful projects while enjoying the flexibility and support to shape your own career.

Qualifications

Who we're looking for

We welcome interest from professionals across the broader Water Resources sector. Whether your expertise lies in technical delivery, project leadership, modelling, planning or design, we'd love to hear from you.

As we continue to grow our teams across Australia and New Zealand, we typically build capability in the following areas:
Flood Engineering
Hydraulic Engineering & Modelling
Surface Water Modelling
Coastal & Marine Engineering
Drainage & Stormwater Engineering
Civil and Water Resources Engineers
Technical Leadership (Technical Leads, Associates & Technical Directors)
Project Management
Design Management

We are interested in hearing from professionals at all career stages, from emerging and developing professionals through to experienced specialists, project leaders and technical experts looking to contribute to some of the region's most significant water projects.

Additional Information

Why you'll love working with us

You'll be joining a team delivering some of the most complex and meaningful water projects across Australia and New Zealand, supported by global expertise, industry-leading technology and a collaborative culture, you’ll also enjoy:
A market-leading pipeline of Water Resources projects
Opportunities to work across Australia, New Zealand and globally
Collaborative, multidisciplinary teams that span design, construction, advisory, and operations phases.
Clear pathways into major projects and clients, technical leadership, project leadership or people leadership roles
Access to industry-leading digital tools and modelling capabilities, including AI driven technology
A culture that values innovation, collaboration and professional growth

In addition, you'll benefit from:
A culture of inclusion, diversity, equity and belonging - where your unique perspectives help us create better outcomes.
Flexible work arrangements, including alternative start/finish times and hybrid work options
Purchase up to 6 weeks additional annual leave
Volunteer and representation leave

Build the career you want

At AECOM, there is no single career path.

You may be looking to deepen your technical expertise, lead major project delivery, grow into people leadership, or expand your experience across different markets and geographies. Whatever your ambition, we'll help you build a career that aligns with your strengths and aspirations.

Join our Talent Network

If you're passionate about shaping the future of water and creating lasting outcomes for communities across Australia and New Zealand, we'd love to hear from you.

Submit your interest, including your preferred location and area of expertise, and we'll connect you with opportunities across our growing Water Resources team.

Join AECOM and help deliver a better world through innovative water solutions.

To support this commitment, all newly hired employees are required to attend an in-person Day 1 onboarding at an AECOM office location as a condition of employment.

AECOM acknowledges the Traditional Owners and Custodians of the lands on which we, our clients and our communities live and work around Australia. We pay our respects to their cultures and to their Elders — past, present, and emerging. We are committed to connecting to Country in our work through meaningful engagement with First Nations peoples and businesses. Find out more about our Australian Reconciliation Action Plan here: https://aecom.com/au/our-vision-for-reconciliation/.

About AECOM

AECOM is the world’s trusted infrastructure consulting firm, delivering professional services throughout the project lifecycle – from advisory, planning, design and engineering to program and construction management. On projects spanning transportation, buildings, water, new energy and the environment, our public- and private-sector clients trust us to solve their most complex challenges. Our teams are driven by a common purpose to deliver a better world through our unrivaled technical and digital expertise, a culture of equity, diversity and inclusion, and a commitment to environmental, social and governance priorities. AECOM is a Fortune 500 firm and its Professional Services business had revenue of $16.1 billion in fiscal year 2025. See how we are delivering sustainable legacies for generations to come at aecom.com and @AECOM.

Freedom to Grow in a World of Opportunity

You will have the flexibility you need to do your best work with hybrid work options. Whether you’re working from an AECOM office, remote location or at a client site, you will be working in a dynamic environment where your integrity, entrepreneurial spirit and pioneering mindset are championed.

You will help us foster a culture of equity, diversity and inclusion – a safe and respectful workplace, where we invite everyone to bring their whole selves to work using their unique talents, backgrounds and expertise to create transformational outcomes for our clients.

AECOM provides a wide array of compensation and benefits programs to meet the diverse needs of our employees and their families. We also provide a robust global well-being program. We’re the world’s trusted global infrastructure firm, and we’re in this together – your growth and success are ours too.

Join us, and you’ll get all the benefits of being a part of a global, publicly traded firm – access to industry-leading technology and thinking and transformational work with big impact and work flexibility. As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we believe in each person’s potential, and we’ll help you reach yours.

jobs.description:
About

This is a Position-Based Test conducted in accordance with CSC Rule 111A.

Application Opening Date: August 25, 2026
Application Filing Deadline: Application filing will be open at least through September 1, 2026 at 11:59PM (PDT), and will close any time thereafter
Location: 505 Paloma Way, Sunol, CA 94586
Recruitment ID: PBT-0922-167137/ RTF0167136-01122585

WHO ARE WE?

San Francisco Public Utilities Commission (SFPUC)

Headquartered in San Francisco, we have 2,300 employees operating across eight counties serving more than 2.7 million customers in the San Francisco Bay Area – 24 hours per day, 365 days per year.

Our Mission
: To provide our customers with high quality, efficient, and reliable water, power, and wastewater services in a manner that values environmental and community interests and sustains the resources entrusted to our care.

Our Vision
: We are an innovative utility leader, recognized for excellent results in service, safety, stewardship, and inclusiveness.

We are an award-winning and industry-leading utilities organization committed to our customers, community interests, and the environment. To learn more about our organization, please visit our website at https://www.sfpuc.org/ .

We are proud of our infrastructure and programs, but most importantly, we value our highly qualified and dedicated workforce which ensures that this vision becomes a reality.

To learn more about working at the SFPUC, visit our career site here .

Role Description

About the Natural Resources and Lands Management Division
: The Natural Resources and Lands Management (NRLM) Division within the Water Enterprise of the SFPUC is responsible for the management of approximately 61,000 acres of Bay Area watershed lands under SFPUC ownership as well as 150 miles of utility right-of-way. The NRLM Division is responsible for managing, protecting, restoring, and monitoring the ecological resources on these lands and environmental compliance for the operations and maintenance of the Hetch Hetchy Regional Water System which serves 2.7 million customers. We are committed to responsible natural resources management that protects and restores viable populations of native species and maintains the integrity of the ecosystems that support them for current and future generations. We strive to become a leader in science-based and collaborative environmental stewardship in order to continue providing high-quality and reliable drinking water to our customers.

About The Position

The Programs and Operations Manager provides daily oversight, leadership and strategic direction for the Alameda Creek Watershed Center (ACWC) , advancing its mission as a hub for public education, community engagement, and watershed stewardship. This position oversees daily operations, including the establishment of clear policies and procedures that support safe, consistent, and high quality operations. The Manager supervises staff and volunteers, fostering a high performing and inclusive team environment. The Manager will be a visible, approachable, and supportive leader who builds trust, develops staff, encourages collaboration, and fosters a positive workplace culture where employees and volunteers can thrive. This position is responsible for overseeing the development of high quality educational and interpretive programs, and ensuring a welcoming and meaningful experience for all visitors. The Manager plays a leadership role in shaping the Center’s public identity, developing partnerships, and leading community engagement efforts that support SFPUC’s mission of service, stewardship, and equity. This position works collaboratively across the Division and the SFPUC on planning and programming efforts that strengthen public understanding of the Alameda Creek Watershed, local ecology, cultural history, and the Hetch Hetchy Regional Water System. The role requires initiative, sound judgment, and a commitment to equity, public service, and environmental stewardship.

Work Schedule:
Tuesday through Saturday with occasional work on evenings and Sundays for special events, subject to change if necessary.

Working Relationship:
This position will report to the Alameda Watershed Resources Manager and will supervise a team of staff and volunteers. Initially this position will supervise the ACWC Facility Coordinator and the Education and Volunteers Coordinator, along with 6 part-time staff and several volunteers. This position will require professional, welcoming and friendly interactions with the public and community/agency partners. This position will require collaboration with the facilities team, communications, staff and managers throughout the division, key staff in PUC, including the Assistant General Manager for the Water Enterprise.

Nature of Work:
Portion of the work duties will be outdoors, exposing the incumbent to inclement weather, potential hazards, and animals common in a natural landscape. The position may stand and/or walk for extended periods of time. Ability to work in a busy, noisy environment. Occasionally may lift and/or push 30 pounds of equipment.

Essential duties and responsibilities include but are not limited to:

Strategic Operations and Facility Management

Provide daily oversight of facility operations to ensure a safe, welcoming, and mission aligned visitor experience.
Lead the development and implementation of operational policies and procedures that guide facility use, visitor services, safety practices, and daily operations.
Oversee the aquarium, exhibits, grounds, and community spaces to ensure safe, high quality and consistent standards.
Direct the care, protection, and organization of collections and interpretive materials.
Oversee safety, security, and emergency preparedness efforts in alignment with SFPUC policies and regulatory requirements.
Coordinate maintenance and repairs with the facilities team and contractors, proactively identifying operational needs and improvements.

Interpretation, Education, and Program Leadership

Provide leadership for the development and delivery of interpretive, educational, and public programs that support SFPUC goals and community needs.
Establish interpretive themes related to watershed ecology, cultural and tribal history, and the Hetch Hetchy Regional Water System.
Develop program guidelines, procedures, and quality standards to ensure consistency and excellence across offerings.
Evaluate program effectiveness and develop summary reports using data and community feedback, supporting continuous improvement.
Maintain subject matter expertise in regional natural and cultural history and SFPUC systems.

Community Engagement and Partnership Development

Lead outreach, community engagement, and communications strategies that increase visibility and participation in ACWC programs.
Build and sustain partnerships with public agencies, schools, community based organizations, tribal representatives and local governments.
Represent the ACWC, the Division, and the SFPUC at public meetings, professional conferences, and community events.
Support initiatives that strengthen community relationships, advance equity, and expand access to programs and services.

Staff and Volunteer Leadership

Build and maintain staff capacity to ensure the ACWC is fully and reliably staffed for public operating hours, programs, and special events
Develop staff guidelines, volunteer protocols, and workflow procedures to support consistent operations.
Lead staff development, performance management, scheduling, and training.
Oversee volunteer recruitment, onboarding, training, and engagement programs.
Provide coaching, and support to staff and volunteers, promoting a collaborative, inclusive, and service oriented culture.

Administration and Strategic Planning

Manage budgets, contracts, procurement, and HR related processes in alignment with SFPUC policies.
Develop and maintain administrative policies and procedures that support efficient, compliant, and transparent operations.
Contribute to strategic planning and the development of long term goals, policies, and operational plans for the Division and SFPUC.
Prepare reports and performance metrics that support accountability and continuous improvement.

Ideal Candidate And Competencies

The ideal candidate will have a demonstrated track record and ability to exercise the following leadership competencies which are critical for success in the role of Alameda and Tuolumne Watershed Resources Manager at SFPUC's Natural Resources & Lands Management Division.

Relationship Management: Builds open, honest, and respectful relationships through effective communication and collaboration techniques. Develops networks and lasting partnerships across boundaries to maintain strategic relationships and achieve common goals. Utilizes a variety of communication approaches to successfully gain support, influence others, and strengthen relationship.

How To Qualify

Minimum Qualifications:
Minimum qualifications reflect the lowest level of acceptable education and/or experience required of an individual such that the individual reasonably could be expected to satisfactorily perform the duties of the position. Candidates must meet all the requirements established by the MQs to be considered for the position.

Education: Possession of a baccalaureate degree from an accredited college or university
Experience: Five (5) years of professional work experience coordinating or directing environmental stewardship, education or related community programs in visitor services, educational programming, interpretive center operations, or community engagement; Experience managing budgets, contracts, or administrative processes and collaborating with community partners, public agencies, educators, or local governments.
License: Possession of a valid and current California driver’s license.

Substitution:
Additional qualifying professional experience may substitute for the education requirement on a year for year basis for up to 2 years. One (1) year is equivalent to thirty (30) semester units/forty-five (45) quarter units.

Note: One year of full-time employment is equivalent to 2000 hours. (2000 hours of qualifying work experience is based on a 40-hour work week.)

Applicants must meet the minimum qualification requirement by the final filing date unless otherwise noted. Applicants who meet the minimum qualifications are not guaranteed to advance through all of the steps in the selection process.

Desirable Qualifications

The stated desirable qualifications may be used to identify job finalists at the end of the selection process when candidates are referred for hiring.

Supervisory experience with staff and volunteers interacting with the public.
Experience developing or implementing policies, procedures, or standard operating guidelines for community, non-profit or public facilities, such as visitor centers or education centers.
Experience supporting operations for a community facility (opening/closing, safety procedures, coordinating maintenance and repairs).
Experience representing and working within a public agency or large governmental or nonprofit organization, such as a park agency, public utility or municipal government.
Leadership experience in supporting interpretive centers or environmental education programs.
Experience developing interpretive exhibits, educational materials, or public programs.
Knowledge of California natural and cultural history, ideally focused on the Diablo Range and Bay Area, including the regional geography, plants and animals.
Experience in community engagement and outreach.
Knowledge of and experience working with local tribes.
Experience collaborating with regional Bay Area community and environmental organizations.
Experience managing contracts.
Experience building partnerships with diverse communities and supporting equitable access to public services.

Every application is reviewed to ensure that you meet the mini

At Apex, we’re building more than a consulting and engineering firm—we’re creating a place where your career accelerates, your contributions matter, and your potential is fully realized. All Apex positions are eligible for annual bonus opportunities, reinforcing our commitment to recognizing and rewarding meaningful contributions that drive our collective growth.

Environmental Scientist/Industrial Hygienist

Locations: Los Angeles or Orange County | ~50% field / 50% remote

Apex is seeking an environmental professional with experience in industrial hygiene to perform asbestos, lead-paint, mold/moisture intrusion, exposure assessment, abatement monitoring, and related industrial hygiene and EHS compliance projects across Southern California.

Employee Benefits

This role offers competitive compensation and a robust benefits package, a balanced mix of fieldwork and report writing, company sponsorship for professional and vocational training, work from home opportunity, collaboration with other industrial hygiene, EHS and other experts, and continued professional development and growth afforded by a rapidly growing national environmental consulting company.

Key Responsibilities

Perform asbestos, lead-based paint (LBP), and microbial/moisture intrusion assessments, along with abatement oversight, with an approximate 50/50 split between field and office work
Conduct safety and compliance assessments in accordance with regulatory standards and client requirements
Support additional environmental services through cross-training, including:
Exposure assessments
Workplace safety evaluations
Stormwater compliance inspections
Soil and groundwater sampling
Noise and air monitoring
Aboveground Storage Tank (AST) inspections

Execute work in alignment with project work plans, standard operating procedures (SOPs), and direction from project managers
Manage scheduling and logistics across all project phases, from coordination and fieldwork through reporting
Prepare clear, accurate, and technically sound client-ready reports using project-specific templates
Collaborate with internal teams to support project delivery and ongoing professional development
Maintain and proactively pursue relevant certifications, including 40-Hour HAZWOPER, CAC, and/or CSST

Qualifications

2+ years of professional experience conducting asbestos surveys and mold/moisture intrusion inspections as an AHERA-accredited inspector (in any state)
Current AHERA certification required
California Certified Asbestos Consultant (CAC) and/or Certified Site Surveillance Technician (CSST) preferred
Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science, Industrial Hygiene, Microbiology, or a related field

What We’re Looking For

Self-motivated and dependable professional who can work effectively with limited supervision
Strong technical writing and critical thinking skills
Solid analytical and math skills for interpreting laboratory data and preparing reports
Excellent attention to detail with the ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines
Strong interpersonal skills and ability to collaborate in a team-oriented environment
Physically capable of performing fieldwork and comfortable working in both field and office settings
Commitment to safety and a strong understanding of safe work practices
Interest in growing within industrial hygiene and expanding into broader environmental consulting services

Why You'll Love Working For Us

Company-subsidized medical and dental.
Company-paid life, short, and long-term disability.
401k match, tuition assistance, and more.
Cross-training and the ability to work on a variety of projects.
Performance-based bonuses or other incentives.
Working with the best and brightest in the industry.

Job description:

About the Company:

Founded in 2006, we are a leading provider of global employment outsourcing solutions that empower businesses with top talents recruitment, cost optimization, ensure compliance, and streamline hiring processes abroad.
With global operations spanning the AP, EMA, LA and NA, ZONBERATION has served over 30 Fortune 500 companies and leading internet corporations across diverse industries, including automotive, e-commerce, tech products, consumer goods, gaming, real estate and finance.

Position Summary:

Our company maintains long-term, stable partnerships with many international corporations. Our work with leading technology companies continues to grow. We have successfully integrated top-tier professionals directly into their operational teams, enhancing their capabilities across multiple functions and contributing to shared success.
We are now recruiting a dedicated and detail-oriented Senior EHS Specialist to join our client’s dynamic tech environment. In this specialist role, you will be responsible for executing comprehensive EHS strategies, maintaining compliance, conducting risk assessments, and supporting the development of a strong safety mindset across all venues, including corporate offices, production facilities, and major events.

Job Description / Scope Of Work
Job Title:
Senior EHS Specialist
Location:
San Jose
Job Type:
Full-time
Job Overview

We are seeking an experienced and proactive Senior EHS Specialist to join our team. This role will be responsible for driving the implementation of EHS strategies, ensuring business operations comply with corporate policies and local regulations, fostering a strong safety culture, and enhancing employee health and safety awareness.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership:
Develop, implement, and continuously improve regional EHS strategies, policies, and procedures in alignment with corporate and business objectives.
Compliance & Risk Management:
Ensure full compliance with all applicable federal, state, and local EHS regulations. Proactively identify, assess, and mitigate EHS risks across operations.
Incident Management:
Lead and oversee incident response, investigation, root cause analysis, and corrective action implementation to prevent recurrence.
Auditing & Inspection:
Plan and conduct regular EHS audits, inspections, and assessments. Track and drive closure of action items to ensure sustained compliance and safety performance.
Program Development & Training:
Design, deliver, and maintain effective EHS programs, training, and communication initiatives for employees at all levels.
Stakeholder Collaboration:
Work closely with cross-functional (XFN) teams—including Operations, HR, Facilities, and Legal—to integrate EHS into business processes and promote initiatives such as wellness, ergonomics, and employee assistance programs.
Reporting & Analysis:
Prepare and present detailed EHS performance reports, metrics, and insights to senior management and stakeholders.
Team Support & Development:
Mentor and support site-level EHS personnel and operational partners, fostering a culture of safety ownership and continuous improvement.
Business Travel:
Willingness to travel nationally and internationally as required to support regional and global business needs.

Qualifications, Skills & Experience

Education:
Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Health & Safety, Occupational Health, or a related field. Advanced degree or professional certification (e.g., CSP, CIH, NEBOSH) is a plus.
Experience:
Minimum of 3–5 years of progressive EHS experience.
Regulatory Knowledge:

WHO ARE WE?

San Francisco Public Utilities Commission (SFPUC)

Headquartered in San Francisco, we have 2,300 employees operating across eight counties serving more than 2.7 million customers in the San Francisco Bay Area – 24 hours per day, 365 days per year.

Our Mission
: To provide our customers with high quality, efficient, and reliable water, power, and wastewater services in a manner that values environmental and community interests and sustains the resources entrusted to our care.

Our Vision
: We are an innovative utility leader, recognized for excellent results in service, safety, stewardship, and inclusiveness.

We are an award-winning and industry-leading utilities organization committed to our customers, community interests, and the environment. To learn more about our organization, please visit our website at https://www.sfpuc.org/.

We are proud of our infrastructure and programs, but most importantly, we value our highly qualified and dedicated workforce which ensures that this vision becomes a reality.

To learn more about working at the SFPUC, visit our career site here.

Job Description

About the Natural Resources and Lands Management Division
: The Natural Resources and Lands Management (NRLM) Division within the Water Enterprise of the SFPUC is responsible for the management of approximately 61,000 acres of Bay Area watershed lands under SFPUC ownership as well as 150 miles of utility right-of-way. The NRLM Division is responsible for managing, protecting, restoring, and monitoring the ecological resources on these lands and environmental compliance for the operations and maintenance of the Hetch Hetchy Regional Water System which serves 2.7 million customers. We are committed to responsible natural resources management that protects and restores viable populations of native species and maintains the integrity of the ecosystems that support them for current and future generations. We strive to become a leader in science-based and collaborative environmental stewardship in order to continue providing high-quality and reliable drinking water to our customers.

About The Position

The Programs and Operations Manager provides daily oversight, leadership and strategic direction for the Alameda Creek Watershed Center (ACWC), advancing its mission as a hub for public education, community engagement, and watershed stewardship. This position oversees daily operations, including the establishment of clear policies and procedures that support safe, consistent, and high quality operations. The Manager supervises staff and volunteers, fostering a high performing and inclusive team environment. The Manager will be a visible, approachable, and supportive leader who builds trust, develops staff, encourages collaboration, and fosters a positive workplace culture where employees and volunteers can thrive. This position is responsible for overseeing the development of high quality educational and interpretive programs, and ensuring a welcoming and meaningful experience for all visitors. The Manager plays a leadership role in shaping the Center’s public identity, developing partnerships, and leading community engagement efforts that support SFPUC’s mission of service, stewardship, and equity. This position works collaboratively across the Division and the SFPUC on planning and programming efforts that strengthen public understanding of the Alameda Creek Watershed, local ecology, cultural history, and the Hetch Hetchy Regional Water System. The role requires initiative, sound judgment, and a commitment to equity, public service, and environmental stewardship.

Work Schedule:
Tuesday through Saturday with occasional work on evenings and Sundays for special events, subject to change if necessary.

Working Relationship:
This position will report to the Alameda Watershed Resources Manager and will supervise a team of staff and volunteers. Initially this position will supervise the ACWC Facility Coordinator and the Education and Volunteers Coordinator, along with 6 part-time staff and several volunteers. This position will require professional, welcoming and friendly interactions with the public and community/agency partners. This position will require collaboration with the facilities team, communications, staff and managers throughout the division, key staff in PUC, including the Assistant General Manager for the Water Enterprise.

Nature of Work:
Portion of the work duties will be outdoors, exposing the incumbent to inclement weather, potential hazards, and animals common in a natural landscape. The position may stand and/or walk for extended periods of time. Ability to work in a busy, noisy environment. Occasionally may lift and/or push 30 pounds of equipment.

Essential duties and responsibilities include but are not limited to:

Strategic Operations and Facility Management

Provide daily oversight of facility operations to ensure a safe, welcoming, and mission aligned visitor experience.
Lead the development and implementation of operational policies and procedures that guide facility use, visitor services, safety practices, and daily operations.
Oversee the aquarium, exhibits, grounds, and community spaces to ensure safe, high quality and consistent standards.
Direct the care, protection, and organization of collections and interpretive materials.
Oversee safety, security, and emergency preparedness efforts in alignment with SFPUC policies and regulatory requirements.
Coordinate maintenance and repairs with the facilities team and contractors, proactively identifying operational needs and improvements.

Interpretation, Education, and Program Leadership

Provide leadership for the development and delivery of interpretive, educational, and public programs that support SFPUC goals and community needs.
Establish interpretive themes related to watershed ecology, cultural and tribal history, and the Hetch Hetchy Regional Water System.
Develop program guidelines, procedures, and quality standards to ensure consistency and excellence across offerings.
Evaluate program effectiveness and develop summary reports using data and community feedback, supporting continuous improvement.
Maintain subject matter expertise in regional natural and cultural history and SFPUC systems.

Community Engagement and Partnership Development

Lead outreach, community engagement, and communications strategies that increase visibility and participation in ACWC programs.
Build and sustain partnerships with public agencies, schools, community based organizations, tribal representatives and local governments.
Represent the ACWC, the Division, and the SFPUC at public meetings, professional conferences, and community events.
Support initiatives that strengthen community relationships, advance equity, and expand access to programs and services.

Staff and Volunteer Leadership

Build and maintain staff capacity to ensure the ACWC is fully and reliably staffed for public operating hours, programs, and special events
Develop staff guidelines, volunteer protocols, and workflow procedures to support consistent operations.
Lead staff development, performance management, scheduling, and training.
Oversee volunteer recruitment, onboarding, training, and engagement programs.
Provide coaching, and support to staff and volunteers, promoting a collaborative, inclusive, and service oriented culture.

Administration and Strategic Planning

Manage budgets, contracts, procurement, and HR related processes in alignment with SFPUC policies.
Develop and maintain administrative policies and procedures that support efficient, compliant, and transparent operations.
Contribute to strategic planning and the development of long term goals, policies, and operational plans for the Division and SFPUC.
Prepare reports and performance metrics that support accountability and continuous improvement.

Ideal Candidate and Competencies:

The ideal candidate will have a demonstrated track record and ability to exercise the following leadership competencies which are critical for success in the role of Alameda and Tuolumne Watershed Resources Manager at SFPUC's Natural Resources & Lands Management Division.

Relationship Management: Builds open, honest, and respectful relationships through effective communication and collaboration techniques. Develops networks and lasting partnerships across boundaries to maintain strategic relationships and achieve common goals. Utilizes a variety of communication approaches to successfully gain support, influence others, and strengthen relationship.

Minimum qualifications reflect the lowest level of acceptable education and/or experience required of an individual such that the individual reasonably could be expected to satisfactorily perform the duties of the position. Candidates must meet all the requirements established by the MQs to be considered for the position.

Experience: Five (5) years of professional work experience coordinating or directing environmental stewardship, education or related community programs in visitor services, educational programming, interpretive center operations, or community engagement; Experience managing budgets, contracts, or administrative processes and collaborating with community partners, public agencies, educators, or local governments.

jobs.description:
**Position overview Position title:** Assistant Professor Salary range: The current salary range for this position is $84,100–$132,900 (9\-month academic year salary), however, off\-scale salary and other components of pay, which would yield compensation that is higher than this range, are offered to meet competitive conditions. Apply by this date to ensure full consideration by the committee.
  
**Final date:** Friday, Oct 9, 2026 at 11:59pm (Pacific Time)
  
Applications will continue to be accepted until this date. Position description
  
The Department of Environmental Science, Policy, and Management (ESPM) at the University of California, Berkeley (UCB) invites applications for a tenure\-track Assistant Professor nine\-month faculty position in the area of Arthropod Biodiversity.
  
Biodiversity lies at the heart of all ecosystems, from the smallest microbiomes to the global expanses of continents, oceans, and the atmosphere. It holds intrinsic value across many dimensions, encompassing species, genes, functions, processes, and cultures, while also providing tangible benefits such as food, medicine, and other natural products. Biodiversity underpins essential ecosystem services, including clean air, water, and soil, and contributes profoundly to human health, cultural identity, and psychological well\-being. Arthropods, which E.O. Wilson famously described as “the little things that run the world,” are the majority of Earth's macrobiota and have recently faced threats from multiple stressors, including climate change, habitat loss and degradation, and cumulative use of agricultural chemicals.
  
Loss of biodiversity, both locally (α\-diversity) and among locations (β\-diversity) is occurring at a rate exceeding our current efforts to discover, document, and understand the species with which we share our planet. These patterns are particularly true for arthropods, with insects showing global declines in populations across multiple orders (sometimes referred to as “insect apocalypse”). At the species level, arthropods now represent 70\-80% of the documented loss of biodiversity. At the same time, many other arthropods are becoming increasingly problematic as invasive species, pests of agriculture and forests, and vectors of plant and animal pathogens. Expertise is needed in understanding drivers of arthropod biodiversity change, including understanding processes leading to resilient populations, communities, and ecosystems.
  
ESPM is a multidisciplinary community of scholars from across the sciences and humanities who conduct research, teaching, and outreach to advance scientific understanding and develop solutions for the world's pressing environmental problems. ESPM is home to a top\-ranked Ph.D. program in environmental science, environmental studies, and ecological/evolutionary biology. Our undergraduate students have a choice of vibrant majors that span the disciplines in the department.
  
ESPM is committed to addressing the family needs of faculty, including dual career couples and single parents. We are also interested in candidates who have had non\-traditional career paths, who have taken time off for family reasons, or who have achieved excellence in careers outside academia. For information about potential relocation to Berkeley, or career needs of accompanying partners and spouses, please visit the Office for Faculty Equity and Welfare's website .
  
**Department :** https://ourenvironment.berkeley.edu/ Qualifications Basic qualifications (required at time of application)
  
Applicants for this position must hold a Ph.D. (or equivalent international degree) or be enrolled in a Ph.D. (or equivalent international degree) granting program at the time of application. Preferred qualifications
  
The successful applicant will develop an internationally recognized research and teaching program focusing on terrestrial arthropod biodiversity in studies of (but not limited to) ecology, arthropod data science, disease biology, community/ecosystem ecology, conservation biology, systematics, evolutionary biology, and biological interventions (including management, removals, biological control, bioremediation, restoration, climate\-adaptation). We encourage applicants whose research contributes to the design, management, and integrated understanding of biodiverse systems, using any of many approaches, including (but not limited to) field surveys, use and integration of natural history collections, ecological manipulations, genomics, AI, and computational biology.
  
The successful candidate will have a doctoral degree in a relevant field such as, but not limited to, biological disciplines (including ecology, evolutionary biology, conservation biology, systematics), environmental sciences, geography, entomology, or related fields. The successful candidate will demonstrate:
  
Expertise in any area of terrestrial (non\-marine) arthropod biodiversity research.
  
Organismal expertise (e.g., ecological, evolutionary, systematic, etc.) in a taxon or group of taxa in any habitat, including but not limited to terrestrial and freshwater ecosystems, including working landscapes.
  
The ability to establish an innovative research agenda in partnership with other disciplines.
  
An interest in participatory research with practitioners and communities and the translation of science into solutions via policy and/or partnerships with government agencies, NGOs, or business.
  
Strong research productivity, potential for external funding, and a commitment to excellence in teaching.
  
Commitment to supporting the success of all students with effective mentoring and innovative classroom pedagogy.
  
Willingness to engage in service and leadership activities within the University and their profession. Application Requirements Document requirement

jobs.description:
Join a growing Queensland environmental team where you will influence major infrastructure, energy, water, defence and resource projects while shaping environmental outcomes for regional communities. We have several long\-term environmental programs in Central QLD and numerous opportunities for work across multiple sectors that will benefit from your environmental expertise.


CQG Consulting (CQG) has recently become part of Beca, one of Asia Pacific’s largest independent advisory, design and engineering consultancies. Together CQG and Beca are strengthening our environmental science, ecology, GIS, stakeholder engagement, planning and approvals capability across regional Queensland. Both CQG and Beca have built their businesses on trusted relationships, outcome\-focused advice and a strong understanding of their clients and the communities in which they work.


**The Opportunity**

We are looking for an experienced **Environmental Scientist** to lead our environmental monitoring programs. The role will see you design and manage monitoring programs, coordinate teams, interpret environmental data, assess compliance and prepare high\-quality scientific reports. Providing technical leadership across monitoring programs, with the opportunity to work on major infrastructure, energy, water, Defence and resource projects.


You will be responsible for the effective delivery of environmental monitoring programs, particularly surface water and groundwater monitoring, and assess the data for Environmental Authority compliance reporting.


While this is primarily a program management, technical and reporting role, you will need a strong practical understanding of environmental field sampling and equipment. You will occasionally undertake or oversee field activities, particularly where technical expertise, troubleshooting or quality assurance is required.


You will also play an important role in ensuring junior staff and field teams are applying appropriate sampling techniques and quality assurance procedures.


You will be a key part of a tight\-knit team of trusted advisors, scientists and environmental specialists, committed to meeting the environmental goals for projects of all sizes. As a team we strive to provide sustainable, culturally sensitive and pragmatic solutions that contribute to making every day better. We also like to have fun along the way, so a good sense of humour will hold you in good stead.


**About You**

You will ideally have a degree or diploma in chemistry, environmental science, environmental engineering, earth science, natural resources or a related discipline, as well as a demonstrated experience managing environmental monitoring programs. Strong practical knowledge and demonstrated experience of surface water, groundwater sampling techniques, will enable you to supervise, mentoring or training junior environmental staff.


You will also have experience in assessing environmental data against Queensland Environmental Authority conditions and regulatory requirements a strong understanding of sampling QA/QC, laboratory analysis and data quality requirements.


Knowledge of the Queensland Environmental Protection Act 1994 and relevant environmental legislation, guidelines and standards is a must, and you will have experience using Monitor Pro or similar environmental data management and reporting software, or the demonstrated ability to quickly learn new systems.


Due to the nature of the work you will enjoy the opportunity to undertake occasional regional and remote travel when required.


**Ready to make the move? / Apply now**

If you want to make every day better, apply online today! If you have any questions, you can find out more about our people and projects by visiting cqgroup.com.au and www.beca.com


*By applying for this role, you consent to authorised hiring managers at Beca and CQG accessing and processing your application and personal information for recruitment purposes.*

*If you are successful in your application for this role you will be employed by CQG, a Beca company.*

jobs.title: Principal Scientist -  Toxicology & Translational Lead (Fully Remote)
jobs.description:
About Lipovectra

Lipovectra Inc. is a preclinical biopharma company developing a pipeline of mRNA-LNP (lipid nanoparticle) therapeutics for in vivo adipose tissue engineering. Its lead asset is slated for first-in-human studies for Q3 2027. The company successfully completed the first tranche of its Series A raise.

Position Summary

We are seeking an experienced, versatile, and detail-oriented Principal Scientist to lead nonclinical strategy across the entire lifecycle of Lipovectra’s proprietary mRNA-LNP therapeutic platform. The role spans the full arc from early exploratory non-GLP research to IND-enabling packages — owning the overall nonclinical development strategy for MLT-001 and future mRNA-LNP programs, including species selection, dose selection, study sequencing, safety margins, toxicology endpoints, recovery design, TK/PK integration and regulatory positioning.

The incumbent will serve as a strategic partner to Discovery and Formulation teams and the official GLP Sponsor Study Monitor. A key focus of this position includes evaluating mRNA-LNP asset efficacy, safety and tolerability in specialized rodent models—specifically Diet-Induced Obesity (DIO) and custom/genetically engineered mouse models (GEMMs) for metabolic and target-driven pipeline expansion—while seamlessly advancing lead programs into definitive GLP repeat-dose studies in minipigs.

Key Responsibilities

Exploratory Non-GLP Toxicology & Pipeline Expansion
Early Candidate Screening: Design and manage non-GLP exploratory efficacy, safety, dose-range finding (DRF), pilot tolerability, and dose-escalation studies (in vitro and in vivo) to support early platform decision-making.
Specialized Mouse Model Strategy: Oversee non-GLP efficacy and safety assessments in complex, disease-relevant rodent models, leveraging DIO mice and custom/transgenic/GEMMs to assess target-mediated liabilities, tissue delivery, lipid accumulation, and metabolic profile interactions.
Indication & Platform Expansion: Partner closely with Discovery Biology, Chemistry, and Formulation Science to evaluate nonclinical efficacy and safety profiles for new therapeutic indications, organ-targeted delivery systems, and novel formulations. Drive alignment with internal platform scientists and external Contract Research Organizations (CRO) contacts on test article specifications, biospecimen collection and processing, biospecimen shipping & logistics, and analytical study design.
Mechanistic Toxicity: Investigate platform-specific liabilities (e.g., innate immune/cytokine response, off-target organ accumulation, complement activation [CARPA], metabolic perturbance, and repeated-dosing tolerability) to establish early safety margins.
Route & Delivery Exploration: Evaluate nonclinical delivery profiles with a primary focus on localized administration, target adipose tissue exposure, systemic exposure, and tissue biodistribution; experience exploring alternative routes (e.g., IV, IM, intratracheal, intrathecal) across exploratory animal models to broaden platform utility is desirable.
GLP Study Oversight, CRO Operations, & Regulatory Monitoring
Sponsor Study Monitor: Serve as the primary technical and regulatory contact overseeing outsourced GLP repeat-dose toxicology, safety pharmacology, developmental/reproductive toxicity (DART), and genotoxicity studies at CROs. Own end-to-end execution of external in vivo and ex vivo study packages, including study tracking infrastructure, test article logistics, biospecimen logistics, and timeline governance across CRO partners. Travel to CRO partners for in-person oversight of critical portions of studies.
Minipig Platform Expertise: Lead the strategic selection, dosing protocol development, toxicokinetic (TK) assessment, and histopathology review for GLP studies in minipig models (Gottingen, Yucatan, or Hanford).
CRO Management & On-Site Audit: Direct study initiation, protocol writing, live-phase monitoring, necropsy inspections, and final report sign-offs while ensuring strict adherence to FDA 21 CFR Part 58 and OECD GLP guidelines.
Sample Integrity & Chain-of-Custody Governance: Establish and own end-to-end sample lifecycle management and chain-of-custody standards for biological matrices (primary tissues, animal organs, plasma, and cell lysates), including cataloging systems, storage conditions, and domestic/international shipping logistics spanning clinical donor sites, external CROs, and internal laboratories.
Data Standards & Protocol Governance: Author, update, and review experimental protocols to embed FDA-compliant data requirements (e.g., CDISC SEND, 21 CFR Part 11) across nonclinical GLP toxicity and IND-enabling studies, setting the standard for regulatory-ready data capture from study initiation.
Cross-Functional Leadership & Regulatory Submissions
Nonclinical Safety Lead: Serve on cross-functional pipeline teams, integrating safety data with pharmacology, pharmacokinetics (PK), and clinical development strategy.
Regulatory Authoring & Engagement: Author and review nonclinical safety summaries for global regulatory submissions, including IND, CTA, IMPD, and Investigator's Brochure (specifically eCTD Module 4). Engage with regulatory authorities (FDA, EMA, etc.) during pre-IND meetings and respond to agency queries regarding nonclinical safety packages.

Required Qualifications

Education: Ph.D. in Toxicology, Pharmacology, Pathology, Veterinary Medicine (D.V.M.), or a related life sciences field OR M.S. in Toxicology/Pharmacology with 7+ years of pharmaceutical/biotech industry experience spanning discovery through GLP toxicology.
7–10+ years of pharmaceutical/biotech industry experience in nonclinical safety assessment.
Proven track record across both non-GLP exploratory/discovery toxicology (pipeline de-risking) and GLP regulatory toxicology.
In-depth scientific knowledge of mRNA therapeutics, LNP formulations, and platform-associated toxicities.
Experience with interpreting biodistribution / tissue exposure data for nucleic-acid therapeutics and/or LNPs.
Hands-on experience working with minipig or non-rodent large animal models, including tailored dosing, clinical pathology, and tissue collection protocols, with deep command of standard in vivo study execution — dosing routes, sampling schedules, necropsy procedures — and downstream biological sample processing workflows.
Extensive experience serving as a Sponsor Study Monitor managing CROs, protocol amendments, and GLP compliance audits, including acting as the primary operational and scientific point of contact for CROs, central labs, and clinical collection partners.
Demonstrated experience establishing and overseeing biological specimen inventory and chain-of-custody systems, including LIMS implementation and cold-chain shipping protocols across multi-site study networks.
Mastery of global nonclinical guidelines (FDA 21 CFR Part 58, OECD GLP, ICH M3(R2), ICH S6, ICH S9).

Preferred Qualifications

DABT (Diplomate of the American Board of Toxicology) certification
Prior experience managing test articles or biological samples derived from nucleic acid therapeutics, LNPs, or novel delivery platforms.
Hands-on or oversight experience using DIO rodent models and custom/transgenic/ GEMMs to evaluate safety, target-mediated effects, and metabolic parameters.
Experience with 3D culture systems, including patient-derived organoids.
Experience in oncology.

Professional Competencies

Senior Environmental Scientist (Specialist)

Sacramento, Oakland, or Lakewood, CA

The Environmental Science Division is responsible for evaluating the vegetation management aspects of utility WMPs, assessing performance in meeting vegetation management-related commitments described in the WMPs, and ensuring that each utility is reducing its risk of igniting a catastrophic wildfire. To this end, Division scientists review regulatory filings and utility procedures, analyze reported data, perform audits, conduct field inspections, publish findings, and engage with the utilities and interested parties. Division scientists serve as subject-matter experts in utility vegetation management and environmental policy related to wildfire risk reduction. Our team of scientists is highly collaborative and works closely with the Compliance Assurance, Electrical Safety Policy, and Data Analytics Divisions.

Under the general direction of the Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisor) in the Environmental Policy Support Branch of the Environmental Science Division, the employee will review and evaluate the vegetation management-related aspects of electric utility Wildfire Mitigation Plans; lead the development of utility vegetation management best practices for wildfire safety; and lead the development of related Guidelines. The employee will also develop and maintain relationships with Federal, State, and local agency partners, and will serve as an environmental science subject matter expert supporting other Energy Safety Divisions. Occasional travel may be required.

Sacramento, CA

The Analyst III serves as a Policy Specialist and will develop standards and regulations related to excavation safety and implementing the Dig Safe Act.
